title: Outlines you can read
subtitle: What outliners are, and how a tree of blocks becomes a paper with its evidence attached.

children.text: An outliner is a writing tool in which a document is a tree of short blocks rather than one long page.

fields.value: A working definition for this article. It describes the shape of the tool, not a claim from a source.

children.text: Each block can hold children, and any branch can be folded away or opened again without changing the text inside it.

fields.value: Describes the common behaviour of outliners. No single source is needed for it.

children.text: Because the structure is explicit, a reader can see at a glance which sentence belongs to which idea.

fields.value: Our interpretation of why explicit structure helps reading. It is not a tested claim.

children.text: The idea of working on text as a structure that can be folded, rearranged and linked is usually traced to Douglas Engelbart’s programme for augmenting human intellect.

fields.value: Cited as the usual origin story. No passage from the report was checked for this article, so open the source before quoting it.

children.text: Later outliners kept the tree but moved it into ordinary files, and OPML became a common way to exchange an outline between programs.

fields.value: The OPML specification defines the exchange format. The claim that it became common is ours and is not measured here.

children.text: In an evidence outliner the tree has a fixed meaning, running from the section down to the exact words a source used.

fields.value: The README gives the five levels verbatim. The sentence restates them without adding a claim.
Section → paragraph → sentence → citation → exact reference.

children.text: Every block can also carry fields, which open as quiet key and value rows under the block instead of a separate form.

fields.value: The design brief states this directly.
Fields reveal inline key:value rows like Tana or Logseq; these are not four separate forms or four boxed cards.

children.text: Tags sit beside the fields, and one sentence can carry several of them, for its role, its support and its topic.

fields.value: Describes this page itself. Hover any sentence to see its tags.

children.text: A source is stored once and every citation points to it, so correcting a reference corrects it everywhere.

fields.value: The README states that quotes and metadata live in shared source blocks.
Quotes and bibliographic metadata are stored in shared source blocks.

blocks.text: Reading an outline as a paper

children.text: The same tree can be shown as an outline for writing or as plain prose for reading, and switching between them leaves the blocks untouched.

fields.value: The README makes this guarantee for the APA view.
Switching views does not discard or rewrite blocks.

children.text: This page is the reading view: the outline is still there, but it stays out of the way until you ask for it.

fields.value: A description of the page you are reading.

children.text: Hovering a sentence shows its piece of the tree in the margin, and that margin is only a projection of the stored blocks.

fields.value: The code comment states that the hover outline is a projection.
The hover outline is a projection, never a second editable copy.

children.text: Nice: this is what makes the evidence feel close.
Choosing a tag in the margin dims every sentence that does not carry it, so you can read one thread of the argument at a time.

fields.value: Try it with the Topic tags on the left.

children.text: Nothing is removed while you do this, and the focus is not saved into the document.

fields.value: Both properties are stated in the project files.
No text is hidden, reordered, or rewritten.
Reading focus is transient UI state, separate from author text and backups.

children.text: Clicking a sentence opens its branch in place, from the citation down to the quoted passage and where that passage sits in the source.

fields.value: Click this sentence to see the behaviour it describes.

children.text: When a source has no checked quote, the page says so instead of inventing one.

fields.value: Open any sentence in the history section to see the unverified state.

children.text: The tags separate what a sentence claims from how well it is supported, which keeps an interpretation from looking like a finding.

fields.value: Our interpretation of why role and support are separate tag families.

children.text: What an outliner does not do
An outliner records where a claim comes from, but it does not check that the source really supports the claim.

fields.value: A limitation of the format. Support decisions are made by people.

children.text: Could the tool flag a quote whose context no longer contains it?
The validator does: a context that does not contain its quote is an error.
A tree also favours one way of dividing an argument, so ideas that cross branches have to be linked with tags or repeated citations.

fields.value: Our interpretation of a known trade-off of hierarchical documents.

children.text: The reading view works best for documents that are finished enough to read, while the outline view remains the place to write.

- Section → paragraph → sentence → citation → exact reference. Blocks retain source-file/line locators, original LaTeX, arbitrary fields and collapse state. Table rows and figure assets are also retained.

**APA view** preserves the full section/paragraph structure and projects the same sentences with author–year citations and a reference list. Select a sentence to see tags, review and evidence (editable only in editing mode). Audit-only evidence links do not insert citations into manuscript prose. Switching views does not discard or rewrite blocks.

Focus counts are unique visible reading blocks, including headings and visual blocks, not only sentences. Paragraph tags apply to their text; figure/table tags include their captions. A heading tag highlights the heading, not its whole section. Search narrows focus matches. Linked references stay prominent; evidence controls remain usable. No text is hidden, reordered, or rewritten. Focus and sidebar folds are session-only and do not alter saved document tags or exports. Printing restores full opacity. See [reading-focus verification](READING_FOCUS.md).
- Quotes and bibliographic metadata are stored in shared source blocks. Editing a shared record updates every linked reference; it does not create inconsistent copies.
The five levels are the whole idea: each one is a block you can open.
A guarantee, not a habit: views are projections of one tree.
